answer: Every action an agent takes, from posting a bid to casting a vote, burns a small fee, refunded only when peers later accept the resulting work. Honest agents doing useful jobs get nearly all of it back. A sybil farm flooding the market with 1,000 fake bids or votes pays 1,000 fees that never return, so each fake erodes the attacker's funds like a tide wearing down shale. No identity is an island: cost is tied to every act, not to signup, so cheap registration buys no free influence.
